comment: Synergistic combinations: factors that compound when taken together (vs simple additive). Each row is a list of factors that combine super-additively, with a strength (high/moderate/low), a label, a mechanism note, and PMID sources.

synergies.label: Vitamin C boosts non-heme iron absorption
synergies.mechanism: Vitamin C reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺ in the duodenum, the form readily absorbed by enterocytes. ~3× absorption of plant-source iron when taken with ≥75 mg vit C.
synergies.context: Especially relevant for vegetarians, women of reproductive age, and anyone with low ferritin.

synergies.label: Piperine boosts curcumin bioavailability ~20×
synergies.mechanism: Piperine inhibits CYP3A4 and glucuronidation in the gut wall, preventing first-pass metabolism of curcumin. Standard supplement formulation pairs curcumin with 5-10 mg piperine.
synergies.context: Without piperine, oral curcumin has very poor absorption. The pairing is what makes anti-inflammatory effects observed in trials replicable.

synergies.label: B6 supports magnesium cellular uptake and sleep / mood pathway
synergies.mechanism: B6 (P5P) is a cofactor for the magnesium-dependent enzymes downstream of magnesium uptake. Combined supplementation outperforms either alone in sleep latency and HPA-axis trials.
synergies.context: Especially relevant for sleep onset issues, premenstrual symptoms, anxiety.

synergies.label: K2 directs calcium absorbed via D into bone, away from arteries
synergies.mechanism: Vitamin D increases intestinal Ca absorption; K2 (MK-7) activates osteocalcin and matrix Gla protein, which deposit Ca in bone and inhibit vascular calcification. Solo high-dose D without K2 may shift Ca toward soft tissue.
synergies.context: Especially relevant if supplementing >2000 IU vitamin D, post-menopause, or with elevated CAC scores.

synergies.label: Insulin spike from carbs increases muscle creatine uptake
synergies.mechanism: Creatine uptake is insulin-dependent at the sarcolemma. Co-ingesting 30-90g carbs raises plasma insulin and roughly doubles muscle creatine retention vs creatine alone.
synergies.context: Most relevant during a creatine 'loading' phase. Less critical at maintenance dose.

synergies.label: L-theanine smooths caffeine: focus without jitters
synergies.mechanism: L-theanine raises alpha-wave brain activity and inhibits glutamate excitotoxicity, blunting the catecholamine surge from caffeine. Combination shows better sustained attention and lower self-reported anxiety than caffeine alone.
synergies.context: Standard ratio: 200 mg L-theanine + 100 mg caffeine. Naturally found in green tea (~50 mg L-theanine + 30 mg caffeine per cup).

synergies.label: Flavanols boost exercise-induced NO bioavailability
synergies.mechanism: Cocoa flavanols (esp. epicatechin) are eNOS substrates. Pre-exercise dose increases flow-mediated dilation and exercise endothelial response above either alone.
synergies.context: Most studied at 200-500 mg flavanols 60-90 min pre-exercise. Don't conflate with sugar-laden chocolate.

synergies.label: Leucine activates mTORC1 muscle protein synthesis
synergies.mechanism: Leucine is the rate-limiting amino acid for the mTOR pathway. Whey naturally contains ~10% leucine; topping up to 3g leucine per dose maximises post-workout muscle protein synthesis, especially in older adults.
synergies.context: Especially valuable in older adults (anabolic resistance) and during caloric deficit.

synergies.label: EPA/DHA + curcumin combine on inflammation pathway
synergies.mechanism: Omega-3s shift eicosanoid synthesis toward anti-inflammatory resolvins; curcumin inhibits NF-κB. Different mechanisms, additive-to-synergistic on inflammatory biomarkers (hs-CRP, IL-6) in trials.
synergies.context: Most relevant for autoimmune, joint, or chronic inflammation conditions.

synergies.label: Prebiotic fiber + probiotic strains co-build microbiome diversity
synergies.mechanism: Fermented foods deliver live bacteria; soluble fiber feeds them. The combination raises short-chain fatty acid production and microbial diversity more than either alone in dietary trials.
synergies.context: Stanford fermented-food trial showed compound effects on inflammatory markers and microbiome diversity above fiber-only or fermented-only arms.

synergies.label: Resistance training + ≥1.2g/kg protein together preserve muscle
synergies.mechanism: Resistance training provides the mechanical signal; protein provides the substrate. Either alone is dramatically less effective than the combination for older-adult sarcopenia outcomes.
synergies.context: Most validated combination in geriatric muscle research — should be near-default advice for over-60s.

synergies.label: Mediterranean pattern + extra-virgin olive oil > diet pattern alone
synergies.mechanism: EVOO polyphenols (oleocanthal, hydroxytyrosol) appear to drive a substantial portion of the Mediterranean diet's CV benefit. The PREDIMED-EVOO arm outperformed the diet-only control.
synergies.context: Quality matters: cold-pressed, unfiltered, polyphenol-rich. Refined oils don't carry the same benefit.

synergies.label: Zinc supplementation needs balanced copper
synergies.mechanism: High-dose zinc (>40 mg/d) blocks copper absorption via metallothionein induction. Chronic high zinc without copper can cause anaemia and neuropathy. Standard ratio: 8-15 zinc : 1 copper.
synergies.context: Synergy here is structural — they need to be balanced, not 'more-of-both'. Worth flagging when users take zinc isolates.

synergies.label: CoQ10 + selenium reduce CV mortality in elderly (KiSel-10)
synergies.mechanism: CoQ10 is an electron-transport antioxidant; selenium is required for glutathione peroxidase. Together they support mitochondrial function in tissue with high oxidative load.
synergies.context: KiSel-10 trial in elderly Swedish adults showed substantial CV mortality reduction over 5+ years with the combination.

synergies.label: Morning light + consistent bedtime co-anchor circadian rhythm
synergies.mechanism: Morning light advances the circadian phase; consistent bedtime maintains it. Together they produce stronger melatonin onset and better sleep architecture than either alone.
synergies.context: Especially valuable for shift workers, night owls trying to shift earlier, and older adults with fragmented sleep.

synergies.label: Combined cardio + strength outperforms either for cardiometabolic outcomes
synergies.mechanism: Aerobic improves mitochondrial density and cardiovascular fitness; resistance preserves lean mass and insulin sensitivity. Combined-arm trials in T2D, obesity, and aging consistently outperform single-modality.
synergies.context: Most-replicated synergy in exercise science. Default for general health.

synergies.label: Soluble fiber + statin: additive LDL-lowering
synergies.mechanism: Fiber sequesters bile acids in the gut, forcing hepatic cholesterol use for re-synthesis; statins block hepatic synthesis directly. Stacked: independent mechanisms with additive LDL reduction.
synergies.context: Adding 10g/day soluble fiber to statin therapy yields ~5-10% additional LDL reduction.

synergies.label: Spermidine + time-restricted eating both raise autophagy
synergies.mechanism: Spermidine is a known autophagy inducer; extended fasting windows independently activate AMPK/autophagy. Theoretical synergy on cellular cleanup; human evidence is preliminary.
synergies.context: Mechanism is plausible but trials with both arms are sparse. Don't oversell.

synergies.label: Walking outdoors > walking indoors for mental health
synergies.mechanism: Same physical activity, but green-space exposure adds a separately-evidenced effect on cortisol, mood, and rumination. Combined: more than additive in depression/anxiety trials.
synergies.context: Especially relevant for users in dense urban environments who can choose where to walk.

synergies.label: Creatine amplifies resistance-training adaptations
synergies.mechanism: Creatine raises the phosphocreatine reservoir, allowing more high-intensity reps and faster recovery between sets. Net effect: more cumulative training volume per session, more hypertrophy.
synergies.context: Effect is modest in untrained individuals but consistent and replicable. Combined-arm trials show ~10-15% more strength gain than training alone.
